title: What If the Wind Twisted a Steel Bridge Apart? Gertie Did

scenes.text: What if ordinary wind could tear down a steel bridge? In 1940, it did.
Only four months after it opened, the Tacoma Narrows Bridge had earned the nickname Galloping Gertie.
On November 7th, the wind blew about 42 miles an hour. Strong, but nowhere near a hurricane.
The deck began twisting from side to side around 10 a.m. and kept going for about an hour.
At 11:10 the roadway fell into the water. The main span had been 2,800 feet long.
Solid steel girders couldn't let the wind pass through. The replacement bridge used an open truss.
